interpretation: Pre-loss focal Thalassia history does not robustly predict the quantitative Braun-Blanquet depth of re-recorded recovery after source abundance, generic habitat headstart, loss-year vegetation continuity, source mixture, stable node and return year are represented. Local history therefore informs return probability and later stability without demonstrably determining return-year abundance.
ecological_update: Recovery dimensions are partially decoupled: historical persistence affects whether Thalassia returns and how stable the return is, whereas the abundance level at return remains largely tied to other state information, especially source abundance.
claim_boundary: Post-hoc quantitative recovery endpoint on an already-opened exact-point return dataset.
Do not claim that longer pre-loss Thalassia history produces deeper quantitative recovery; the frozen coefficient interval overlaps zero.
The positive point estimate is descriptive and does not replace the failed support rule.
Braun-Blanquet is ordinal abundance, not percent cover, biomass or ecosystem function.
Do not interpret the supported history effects on return probability/stability as evidence that the same mechanism controls recovery abundance.
Do not retune history definitions, controls, quantitative inclusion, model or support threshold to rescue a recovery-quality legacy effect.
